Not the 7.5% of `annual_rate_review_terms`.

Effective date **2027-01-01**: normal effective month 1 (`annual_rate_review_terms`); notice clock 2026-10-09 + 60 = 2026-12-08 ≤ 2027-01-01; guarantee (12 months from 2019) long ended; status active; prior increase effective 2026-01-01, so at most one in any 12-month period holds.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root: advance payment of the coming month (customer's own write, `make_advance_payment_0a0cd4e1`).

- Hop A (root → annual increase recorded). Visible sentence, `coming_month_statement` § Fee in effect: "The advance amount is not worked out until the residency record shows, as its fee in effect, the fee taking effect on the first day of the coming month under any annual increase whose notice period has already run." Record: `rate_notice_date 2026-10-09`, `proposed_monthly_service_fee 4279.39`, `monthly_service_fee 3962.4` effective 2026-01-01 → the record does not show the January 2027 fee; notice clock 60 days (`annual_rate_review_terms`) ran on 2026-12-08. Searching "fee in effect" / "annual increase" → `annual_increase_entry`: "Recording the increase replaces the contracted base monthly service fee in effect on the residency record with the recorded fee, sets the rate effective date ..." — the write that brings the state about. Mark: **state-derived**.
- Hop B (root → late fee entry for 2026-12). Visible sentence, `open_account_balance_coming_month`: "The advance amount is worked out only after the ledger carries a late fee entry for the billing period of the latest monthly fee charge whenever that period's grace period has ended with a past-due amount at or above the minimum that draws a late fee." Records: latest monthly fee charge period 2026-12 posted 12-01, grace ended end of 12-11; past-due 5147.40 via the returned-payment branch (≥ 100.00); no late fee entry for 2026-12 on the ledger. `late_fee_assessment_entry`: "Posting the late fee writes one late fee entry on the residency ledger for the billing period given". Mark: **state-derived**.
- Neither `annual_increase_entry` nor `late_fee_assessment_entry` (nor their computation/factor documents) states a prerequisite of its own, so the tree has depth 1, two leaves, no order between A and B.

Handling order: {A, B} in any order → root.

- "Do only what was asked" (pay 5182.40 + 5007.40 = 10189.80, or similar) is excluded by the two blocked-side sentences above: the advance amount "is not worked out until" the record shows the increase and "only after" the late fee entry exists; both states are false at the frozen moment.
- Closest alternative ceiling (7.5% contractual) excluded by `entrance_plan_increase_ceilings` occupied/fee-for-service row; lifecare 4.0% excluded by background + entrance plan pricing table (LifeChoice = fee-for-service).
- Alternative past-due 0.00 (no late fee) excluded by `past_due_returns_and_credits` branch 1.
- Alternative returned-fee reduction 17.50 excluded by the Q&A definition of an ACH autopay payment (entry posted with the ACH autopay method within the month) — the visible text closes this boundary; I note the reading the "never received" language in another document could suggest, but it is scoped to the past-due amount only.
- Alternative "noticed fee is recorded" excluded by `increase_ceiling_and_floor` "The noticed fee exceeds the ceiling fee | The ceiling fee".
- Alternative payment owner (agent draws) excluded by `advance_payment_entry` "customer-side tool".
- Alternative "closing payment" excluded: no notice of termination on the residency.
- Minor findability note: `entrance_plan_increase_ceilings` says the plan's contract type is "read from the customer's Entrance Fee Agreement record", but the record carries only `variant_name`; the type is resolved through the background and `docs/entrance/plan_pricing_schedule`. Reachable, so not a blind-side failure.
